response.sql: WITH order_avg AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), bench1 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS b1 FROM order_avg), kept1 AS (SELECT o.ordersmark, o.avg_fill, o.avg_fill - b.b1 AS excess1 FROM order_avg o CROSS JOIN bench1 b WHERE o.avg_fill > b.b1), bench2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS b2 FROM kept1), final AS (SELECT k.ordersmark, k.avg_fill, k.excess1, k.avg_fill - b.b2 AS excess2 FROM kept1 k CROSS JOIN bench2 b WHERE k.avg_fill > b.b2) SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS avg_fill_final, AVG(excess1) AS avg_first_excess, AVG(excess2) AS avg_second_excess FROM final;

assumptions.assumption: GROUP BY ordersmark puts all executions with NULL ordersmark into one shared group, as the request asks.
AVG(fillcount) skips NULL fill quantities (the 'ignore missing' rule) and keeps 0 values (the 'zero counts as 0' rule).
A group whose fillcount values are all NULL has a NULL average, so it is excluded from both benchmarks and from the threshold filters.
'Above' means strictly greater than the benchmark, and the per-order averages are unweighted (each order counts once in the benchmark means).
The final row's first and second excess averages are taken over the final orders only, not over all orders kept at the first stage.
No rounding is applied, as the request specifies. The SQL is written in standard SQL (CTEs, CROSS JOIN, AVG) because the dialect is not specified.
